key_insight: Structure-preserving Fourier quantum circuits can simulate acoustic and Dirac wave dynamics on real trapped-ion hardware while preserving physically meaningful observables at large encoded scales.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that near-term quantum processors can track reduced wave-equation metrics, such as subdomain kinetic energy, for grids as large as 1024 points in 1D and 32×32 in 2D without reconstructing full fields.
method: Fourier-based, structure-preserving quantum circuits for 1D and 2D acoustic wave equations and Dirac dynamics with variable mass
Direct estimation of subdomain kinetic energy from measurement samples instead of full-state field reconstruction
Benchmarking on the Quantinuum H2-2 trapped-ion processor with compiled circuits and product-formula evolution
evidence_signal: Across all tested problems, the hardware results matched classical kinetic-energy dynamics with mean absolute errors between 5.9×10^-3 and 2.4×10^-2.
watch_item: Compiled gate counts grow roughly quadratically with the number of grid qubits, and the cost can also increase with more product-formula steps, which may limit scalability.
paper_title: Structure-Preserving Quantum Simulation of Wave Equations on a Trapped-Ion Processor
